clue.text: Face section D — it's a commando force

blocks.note: the chin is one section of the face
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A briefing names a stretch of front, Section D, and says which elite unit holds it.
explanation.walkthrough: The apparent link phrase it's is itself part of the wordplay; only the a joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chindits were the British long-range jungle troops Orde Wingate led behind Japanese lines in Burma during the Second World War.

clue.text: Best man's bloomer if he omits end of speech.

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter of the next word is used
the clue says the winner becomes a flower once he leaves a letter out, so that letter sits inside the flower's name

blocks.note: campion is a pink or white wild flower, and a bloomer is something that blooms
the last letter of speech

explanation.surface: A wedding best man makes a blunder by leaving off the end of his speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer looks like a gaffe, matching the wedding speech; here it is a flower. The clue runs backwards: take H out of the answer and you are left with CAMPION.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is the winner, the top person in a contest, so he is literally the best man.

clue.text: On the rocks near Iow? Vessel's front caught

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept
something caught is held inside, so this letter is trapped within the other piece

blocks.note: IoW is the Isle of Wight, and the strait beside it is the Solent, so near it is IN SOLENT
the first letter of vessel

explanation.surface: A ship has run aground off the Isle of Wight, its bow stuck fast.
explanation.walkthrough: On the rocks suggests a shipwreck, which the rest of the surface supports, but it is the slang for being broke. The Solent is the channel between the Isle of Wight and mainland Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A business on the rocks is financially ruined, unable to pay its debts, which is exactly what insolvent means.

clue.text: Coach providing courses for those training

definitions.text: Coach providing courses for those training

blocks.clueFragment: Coach providing courses for those training
blocks.note: surface reading: a sports coach running classes for people in training
setter's reading: a railway coach serving meal courses to people travelling by train

explanation.walkthrough: Coach and courses both point to teaching; read coach as a railway carriage, courses as parts of a meal, and training as going by train.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant car on a train, where passengers sit down to a meal, is called a dining car or diner.

clue.text: Three bank holidays for the rest of its crew?

definitions.text: Three bank holidays for the rest of its crew?

blocks.note: surface reading: three public holidays when the banks close

blocks.clueFragment: Three bank holidays for the rest of its crew?
blocks.note: setter's reading: an ancient warship rowed from three banks of oars, where one bank resting gives its oarsmen a break

explanation.walkthrough: Bank holiday is a British public holiday; here each bank is a tier of oars on a galley, and a bank on holiday lets those rowers rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was a Greek or Roman galley with oarsmen seated in three tiers, one above another.

clue.text: Such a word usually is

blocks.note: surface reading: a vague remark that some kind of word is commonly so
setter's reading: the word usually is itself an example of the part of speech wanted

explanation.walkthrough: Usually reads as part of the sentence, but it is the specimen: the clue says such a word as this one is a certain kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like usually, which modify verbs or whole sentences and often end in -ly, belong to this grammatical class.

clue.text: Found at card-table on board?

blocks.note: surface reading: a seat drawn up to a table for playing cards
setter's reading: a pack of cards followed by a seat at a table, and the thing is found on board ship

explanation.walkthrough: A pack of cards is a deck, and what you find at a table is a chair; together they make the folding seat found on a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The folding canvas seat used for lounging on a ship's deck or a beach takes its name from the deck.

clue.text: Take sweetheart and run

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so only the central letter is kept

blocks.note: the middle letter of sweet
to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A lover snatches their beloved and the pair dash off together.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweetheart is one word on the surface; split it, and its heart is the middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly with a lover, usually in order to marry.

clue.text: Next to King or Queen,- one .- 14

blocks.note: first meaning: the chess piece that starts beside the king and the queen
second meaning: a senior cleric, whose title comes from the Greek for one who oversees, the answer to 14

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue is garbled after one; 14 is OVERSEE, and the word comes from Greek episkopos, overseer.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess this piece stands beside the royal pair at the start; in the church it names a cleric who supervises a diocese.

clue.text: Nine-a-side dance? .

blocks.note: surface reading: a team sport with nine players per team
setter's reading: an old board game in which each player has nine pieces shares its name with an English folk dance

explanation.walkthrough: Nine men's morris is a board game in which each side has nine counters; the word also names the English folk dance with bells and sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Morris dancing is traditional English folk dancing by teams called sides, so the name fits both game and dance.

clue.text: Would the Mikado have fired its perpetrator?

definitions.text: Would the Mikado have fired its perpetrator?

blocks.clueFragment: Would the Mikado have fired its perpetrator?
blocks.note: surface reading: whether the emperor would sack the offender for some crime
setter's reading: the Mikado sings of making the punishment fit the crime, so the culprit of this crime would be set on fire

explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado the emperor's aim is to let the punishment fit the crime; fired means burned, not dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property, so a fitting penalty would be burning.

clue.text: Decoration for Brand x

blocks.note: a branding iron marks cattle, so brand can mean iron
the letter x is a cross

explanation.surface: An award is named after a product, Brand X, as in an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: Brand X is the stock advertising name for a rival product; split it into an iron and a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a Prussian and German military medal for bravery, a decoration worn by soldiers.

clue.text: Quiet sort of arboreal animal-

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so these letters come in a different order

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
the eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Some tree-dwelling creature is described as quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Arboreal looks like a description of the animal, but it is the fodder; the beast is the least tree-dwelling of all.
explanation.definitionFit: The white bear of the Arctic is a large carnivorous mammal, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Part of sacred orthodoxy

indicators.note: part of a phrase is a run of its letters, so the answer is spelt inside the following words

blocks.note: spelt out across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A statement of belief forms one element of established religious teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a formal statement of religious belief, and so is one element of orthodox faith.

clue.text: View from above across deep sound

indicators.note: a sound is what is heard, so the word is wanted for how it is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: to go across something is to go over it
the deep is the sea

explanation.surface: From a height one looks out across a deep stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound looks like a body of water to go with deep, but it signals a spoken likeness.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise, literally to watch over a task from a position above it.

clue.text: No such lack for Alice in rabbit-hole.

definitions.text: No such lack for Alice in rabbit-hole.

blocks.note: surface reading: Alice was not short of something

blocks.clueFragment: No such lack for Alice in rabbit-hole
blocks.note: setter's reading: Alice's tumble down the rabbit-hole was famously long, so it was anything but brief

explanation.walkthrough: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the drop down the rabbit-hole lasts so long she wonders if she will come out at the Antipodes; the answer splits as the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is a deficit, an amount by which something falls short, and read in two words it is a brief drop.

clue.text: Crustacean found in Southern rivers

definitions.note: scampi is strictly plural, the Italian name for Dublin Bay prawns, but is used for one dish or creature

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for southern
the Cam is the river through Cambridge; the scanned clue shows nothing certain for the last two letters, so the second river here is unconfirmed

explanation.surface: Some shellfish is said to live in the rivers of the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Only part of this parse is sure: S plus the river CAM gives SCAM, and the remaining PI is not accounted for by any river in the scanned text, which may have lost a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are Norway lobsters, also called Dublin Bay prawns, small edible shellfish of the lobster family.

clue.text: Introducer of motion to support No. Ten perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps marks the letters as only one possible arrangement, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: a prop supports
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tables a motion backing Number Ten, the Prime Minister's office.
explanation.walkthrough: No. Ten, Downing Street, suggests the Prime Minister, but its letters are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In a debate the proponent is the person who proposes, putting the motion forward for discussion.

clue.text: Chap showing momentary brilliance at Rugby?

definitions.text: Chap showing momentary brilliance at Rugby?

blocks.note: a flash is a moment of brilliant light
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A player shows a brief spark of genius on the rugby field.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is the school, not the game: Flashman is the bully at Rugby School in Tom Brown's Schooldays.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashman is the cowardly bully of Thomas Hughes's novel set at Rugby School, later revived as a hero by George MacDonald Fraser.

clue.text: Do in

blocks.note: first meaning: a party or reception held at one's house
second meaning: present in one's own house rather than out

explanation.walkthrough: Do is the informal word for a party, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An at-home is a social gathering held in a host's house, and to be at home is to be in.

clue.text: Plays in new version of this for instance

indicators.note: a new version of a word reorders its letters

blocks.note: taken as written: the letters added to this answer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drama is staged in a modern adaptation of some work, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: this is the answer, and a new version of the answer with in added is instance. So take in from instance and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a part is to perform it on stage, so enacts means acts out or performs.

clue.text: Humorist calling for firmer suspension of driver

blocks.note: what a driver drives
body roll, a car leaning on corners, is the thing that calls for stiffer suspension

explanation.surface: A comic writer campaigns for stiffer springs on motorists' cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Read calling for firmer suspension as a description: the sway of a vehicle that needs stiffer springs, belonging to a driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll, author of the Alice books and nonsense verse, is one of the great English comic writers.

clue.text: Seven keys greengrocer has

definitions.note: an item a greengrocer has: the clue gives a description, not a noun

blocks.note: seven musical keys in a row, every letter one of A to G

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper selling fruit and veg carries seven keys on a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Keys are musical, named by the letters A to G, and seven of them spell a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabbage is a leafy green vegetable, standard stock on the counter of any vegetable seller's shop.

clue.text: Cunning, we hear, but means little disrespect

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken form, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: sleight is cunning or dexterity, as in sleight of hand
meaning: small, slender
meaning: a snub or insult

explanation.surface: A sly trick is mentioned, but it amounts to only minor rudeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight as an adjective means small or slender, and as a noun it means a snub or insult.

clue.text: Great composer? Hear, hear

indicators.note: the second hear asks for how a word is heard, a spoken likeness

blocks.note: list is an old word for listen, so to hear

explanation.surface: Someone applauds a great composer with cries of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Hear, hear looks like parliamentary applause; list, an archaic verb meaning to listen, sounds like the Hungarian pianist and composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt, the nineteenth-century Hungarian pianist and composer, is ranked among the great Romantic composers.

clue.text: Place for landing or take-off

blocks.note: first meaning: a narrow runway for aircraft, an airstrip
second meaning: to undress, removing one's clothes

explanation.walkthrough: Landing and take-off both sound like flying, but take-off here is a verb about clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip is a long narrow piece of ground for aircraft, and to strip is to remove clothing.

clue.text: Shot with craft on course

blocks.note: surface reading: a boat or aircraft holding its heading
setter's reading: a golf stroke played with great skill on the links, scoring three under par on a hole

explanation.walkthrough: Craft suggests a vessel and course a heading; on a golf course the rarest skilful score is named after a seabird, three strokes under par.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an albatross means completing a hole in three strokes fewer than par, a feat of exceptional skill.

clue.text: Ban upset . cricketer getting a pair

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: a bat is a batsman
a pair in cricket is two ducks, scores of nought, in one match

explanation.surface: A batsman bags a pair, out for nought twice, and is banned in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset looks like the cricketer's mood; it turns the word around. A pair in cricket is scoring zero in both innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is a prohibition, a ban on something by custom or religion.

clue.text: Giant hog

blocks.note: first meaning: the giant of Rabelais's sixteenth-century tales
second meaning: a glutton, as that giant was famous for his appetite

explanation.walkthrough: Giant hog reads as a big pig; each word separately names the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantua is the huge, insatiably hungry giant in Rabelais, so the name suits both a giant and a greedy eater.

clue.text: Variety of amber or yellowish fish

indicators.note: a variety of something is another form of it, so these letters take another order

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A fish is described as either amber in colour or yellowish.
explanation.walkthrough: Amber looks like a colour beside yellowish, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The freshwater bream is a deep-bodied fish with bronze or yellowish flanks.

clue.text: Overthrow disheartens Times readers ?

indicators.note: to dishearten is literally to take out the heart, so the middle letters are removed

blocks.note: Top People take The Times was the newspaper's famous advertising slogan

explanation.surface: A coup dismays the readership of this very newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times advertised itself with the slogan Top People take The Times; remove the three middle letters of that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple a ruler is to bring them down from power, which is what overthrow means.

clue.text: Produced note, for example, to change 50 per cent of score

indicators.note: to change a word is to alter it, so its letters swap places

blocks.note: B is a musical note
e.g. is the abbreviation of for example
the two letters swapped round
a score is twenty, and half of that is ten

explanation.surface: A composer writes a note as an example of how to alter half a musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: Score suggests music, alongside note, but here it is the number twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Begotten is the past participle of beget, to father or bring into being, so it means produced.
